acceptance.criterion: Each drops below the 8 KB anyComponentStyle budget
acceptance.evidence: pnpm build before this PR's edits: guest-manager.scss exceeded maximum budget by 3.19 kB (11.19 kB of 8 kB) — matches T355's own measured figure. After this PR's edits (typecheck/lint/test/build all re-run clean, see checks below): exceeded by 3.69 kB (11.69 kB of 8 kB) — a small net INCREASE. Isolated the cause with a dedup-only compile (respond-to() conversion + the two genuine-duplication extractions, no token substitution): 14,151 bytes raw CSS vs 14,261 pre-migration (a real, if small, reduction). Compiling with the token substitutions this same task bullet also requires ("tokens for raw px", CLAUDE.md hard rule 3) instead measures 14,735 bytes — var(--space-N) (14 chars) is textually longer than a literal Npx (2-5 chars) at every one of the ~30 sites converted, and that cost exceeds the dedup savings several times over.
acceptance.notes: Per the task's own explicit instruction ("do not gut the screen to hit the number and do not silently miss the bullet... A correct migration that is over budget is a better outcome than a screen rewritten past what this task authorizes"), the token conversion was kept (it is mandated by the same bullet and by CLAUDE.md hard rule 3) and the shortfall reported honestly rather than reverted to chase the number. See decisions_needed[] — this generalizes config-manager's own finding (T343.json) into a clearer structural tension between ADR-0041 §6 (tokens) and §7 (the byte budget).

acceptance.evidence: No interactive browser available in this environment. Verified via Playwright (scratch specs, run and deleted — not committed, per this task's own instruction on how T355 handled the same limitation): 6 combinations of theme (terracotta/mauve/verdeagua) x width (360px/1280px) all passed (header/nav/table/footer render, data-theme attribute correct) with full-page screenshots taken and visually reviewed by hand (all 4 sampled screenshots showed correct rendering, no overlap/clipping, correct theme colors); 3 locale sanity checks (es/en/fr, via signInAsCouple + localStorage 'language' + fresh navigation, matching T352/T355's own convention) all passed (translated header text present, non-empty).
acceptance.notes: This is a Playwright-driven check against real WebKit/Chromium engines, not a physical device — stated plainly per CLAUDE.md's own instruction not to claim a device check that wasn't done. The underlying change is CSS-value-preserving (respond-to() compiles to the identical @media rule; every token substitution maps to the exact pixel value it replaced; the two extractions are structurally equivalent CSS) so the a-priori regression risk was low, and the sweep found none.

acceptance.criterion: guest-manager's slice additionally carries the coverage T355 could not commit — a spec asserting .scrolled's background/box-shadow appears on /guests once the list has scrolled, and that head and foot hold position
acceptance.evidence: New e2e/layout/guest-manager-scrolled-header.spec.ts. Proven failing first: run against a worktree at 58935c7 (the commit immediately before hub ADR-0043/e11d826, when /guests' main was overflow-y:clip and never scrolled) — failed on all 5 projects with "main did not move when scrolled" (the header's dead-scroll defect ADR-0043 §5's addendum describes). Run against current code: 5/5 projects pass. Background assertion is width-conditional (checked in the spec's own header comment): below 900px the header is transparent until .scrolled supplies --surface-card; at/above 900px screen-header.scss's own @media block gives header a solid background unconditionally, so there is nothing to change there — box-shadow (supplied only by .scrolled, at every width) is the assertion that holds unconditionally. Uses expect.poll for the post-scroll read because header's CSS transition (0.2s) meant an immediate getComputedStyle read could land mid-transition (reproduced once during authoring, fixed before commit).
acceptance.notes: pinned-regions.spec.ts (existing, T341) already covers the generic pinned head/foot invariant; this spec re-asserts it only as its own guard clause, not to duplicate that file's coverage.

decisions_needed.question: guest-manager.scss is now 11.69 kB against an 8 kB anyComponentStyle budget (was 11.19 kB before this migration), and the token-substitution half of a correct ADR-0041 §6 migration made the gap larger, not smaller, because CSS custom property references are textually longer than the literal px values they replace. This is the same open question config-manager's T343 slice already raised (tasks/28-phase-x-layout-layer/reports/T343.json decisions_needed[0]) but demonstrated more starkly here. How should the remaining ~3.7 kB be closed, given T344 depends on all four T343 screens being under budget?
options: Extract a genuinely reusable piece into its own component — the strongest candidate is the loading-skeleton block (~55 lines: .skeleton, .stat-bar, .count-bar, .name-bar, .caption-bar, .status-bar, .cell-bar, .dietary-bar, .footer-bar), which rides on real settled elements per _primitives.scss's own skeleton-bar mixin doc. Genuinely reduces guest-manager.scss's own anyComponentStyle count; costs a new component/directive and a review of whether a shared 'skeleton row' pattern would also help milestones/seating-plan (both also over budget) — a design-system question this task cannot answer alone.

Raise guest-manager's own anyComponentStyle budget via a per-file override (angular.json), on the same terms T344 already grants config-manager: 'a complete, correct migration' whose remaining gap is not shell/scroll CSS. Cheap and immediate; is a second per-path override (T344's own text calls a second one 'a hub decision under §7 as amended').

Reconsider whether hard rule 3's token substitution is worth doing for already-baselined violations at all, given it demonstrably works against ADR-0041 §7's own budget goal on this file. Not something this task is authorized to decide unilaterally — it would mean treating 'tokens for raw px' as optional during a budget migration, contradicting this task's own explicit instruction.

Leave it over budget and scope T344 to exclude both config-manager and guest-manager (or delay T344 until a later, separately-scoped cleanup covering both). No new work now; T344's acceptance text needs amending regardless once a second screen hits the same wall.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Extract the skeleton block (option 1) if a shared 'loading skeleton row' pattern is judged to have a real home in the design system — it is the most self-contained, least risky piece of this file, and milestones/seating-plan (also over budget, also table/list screens) are plausible co-beneficiaries. Failing that, option 2 (a second per-file ratchet) is honest and consistent with T344's own precedent for config-manager, but it is a hub-level call under ADR-0041 §7 as amended, not a repo decision.
